tg.conclusion: Reviewed Telegram v0.105.0 to v0.106.0 with the exact published command contract: `reactions list <chat> <message> [query]` (newest first, `reaction:<emoji>`, --limit and --cursor, read only, permission `reactions.list`, refused with `reactions.broadcast` in a channel and `reactions.list-hidden` where the chat hides the list); `contacts info` is now `contacts show`, which also answers --offline and takes --with-notes; phone numbers are shown whole and `--show-phone` is gone, `--hide-phone` leaves the number out of `account show`, `account update` and `contacts show`; a shared contact card shows its name and phone; `contacts sync` saves phones; inbox, review and search answers carry `sender_is_me`; the agent skill is listed on ClawHub as `wirecat-tg`; the `mcp serve --profiles` examples no longer name a profile. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.92.0 and none of its planned items (chat notes, emoji reaction rankings, remaining max parity, location messages) shipped: `reactions list` names who reacted, it does not add per emoji counts to rankings.

max.conclusion: Reviewed MAX v0.85.0 to v0.86.0 with the exact published command contract (Core 0.478.0): `max mcp serve` with no profile refuses (exit 2) and lists the profiles; `--profiles a,b` or `--profiles all` serves several from one server, also for `--http`, `mcp server start|stop|status`, `mcp revoke` and `mcp config`; `contacts show` replaces `contacts info`, phone numbers print whole and `--hide-phone` leaves them out (`account show`, `account update`, `contacts show`); `sender_is_me` on messages, inbox, review and search hits; the agent skill is `wirecat-max` on ClawHub. RU commands and EN/ES changed guides, changelog and technical reference reviewed. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.76.0; none of its planned items shipped in these releases.

drive.conclusion: Reviewed Google Drive v0.45.1 to v0.61.0 with the exact published command contract. New commands: `drive doctor`, `drive skill`, `drive mcp config|add|check`, `drive documents check` and `drive config migrate`; `mcp serve --tools` is gone (use `commands --json` and `mcp check`). Sign-in: `session start --client-id` with the secret in `DRIVE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, or the saved `google_client_id` setting, picks your own Google app (`DRIVE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` wins over the setting); with no reachable keyring the login falls back to a private file and answers `storage: "file"`; a `--client-file` that other users can read is refused; a run with moved folders never removes the owner's sign-in. The installation guide no longer describes the WireCat app's Google review or the 100-user limit: it says what to do when Google refuses the sign-in. Error codes renamed in 0.61.0 (`api.disabled`, `oauth.*`, `sign-in.client-rejected`, `file.not-a-file`, `profile.locked`, `profile.busy`) and `doctor --json` reports `oauth_client`. Remote login waits 30 seconds after five wrong codes instead of locking until restart. RU/ES changelog (release notes kept in English, as before), commands, configuration, installation, recipes, remote, roadmap, scenarios, search, security and troubleshooting reviewed; the site's drive install prompt (lib/words.ts) no longer warns about the unverified-app screen. Roadmap: the in-progress Google app review was dropped, not shipped; `mirrors watch` as a background service stays next and both later items are unchanged.

wa.conclusion: Reviewed released WhatsApp 0.21.0 (Core 0.506.0/Base 0.67.0), covering 0.18.0 to 0.20.0. 0.18.0 transcribes an audio file someone sent, not only a voice note (AAC/M4A need ffmpeg, over an hour is refused). 0.19.0 makes tags list name: ignore case in any alphabet (store v38) and lists gcal under Works with. 0.20.0 finds notes, documents and contact notes by any part of a word in any case, refuses searches under three characters and moves the store to v40. 0.21.0 records each engine request and Graph call as a wire line in events.jsonl (message id only, never a chat id or phone number), adds page.total to search messages, makes --discover search by meaning for explicit syntax and rank a narrow chat:/date: filter's own messages, answers meta.complete: false for a chat held only in part, and refuses an unknown transcribeWith. RU/ES changelog, attachments, commands, diagnostics, remote and search reviewed. The roadmap is unchanged since 0.17.0: reactions you send are still not kept in the local store, and channel files, business labels, the guide command, more files per message and communities stay planned. Earlier: Reviewed WhatsApp v0.11.0 to v0.17.0 with the published changelog and command contract: `reactions list <chat> <message>` (newest first, `reaction:<emoji>`, --limit and --cursor) lists who reacted from what the local store received (history push, serve and watch), because WhatsApp has no request for older reactions; a reaction sent with `reactions add` or one that arrived while nothing listened is missing, and a channel refuses it with `reactions.broadcast`. `contacts info` is now `contacts show` (--offline), `--show-phone` is gone and `--hide-phone` is the opt-in; a shared contact card shows name and phone. RU/ES changelog, commands, cli-contract, archive, bot, configuration-reference, diagnostics, limits, mcp, people, query-language, recipes, remote, sessions and usage reviewed. The roadmap plans are unchanged: reactions you send are still not kept in the local store, so that item stays planned, as do channel files, business labels, the guide command, more files per message and communities.

gcal.conclusion: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.21.0 (Core 0.600.0/Base 0.80.8). 0.21.0 adds schedule --notify-on and --deliver-to (schedule agent also --model and --max-cost-per-day), and session start --client-id with the google_client_id setting to choose your own Google app (order: --client-file or --client-id, GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, the profile's then the defaults' google_client_id, WireCat's app; the secret only from GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET; config set refuses google_client_id to an agent). A write cut short by Ctrl-C ends as outcome_unknown (exit 14), not cancelled. Security: every api events method also checks the key of the matching events command, reads included, on --dry-run, api show (also_checks) and MCP, and a patch to cancelled also checks events.delete; checked on the 0.21.0 build with an isolated profile, no sign-in: api show calendar.events.delete lists also_checks events.delete, and api calendar-events-delete --dry-run is refused with access.denied once events.delete is deny. mcp serve --permission api.<method>=deny now stops the events writes that call that method. A Google call no longer holds the finished command for 30 seconds. gcal's own installation, configuration, usage, troubleshooting and roadmap pages now say every package carries WireCat's Google app and that Google may refuse a sign-in through it, so the five 0.20.0 portal corrections for those pages are retired; the changelog correction for 0.20.0's two old reason names stays, since that section is unchanged. One new EN correction rewords "unset the secret to use WireCat's app" in troubleshooting, which docs:versions read as an editorial phrase. EN/RU/ES pages reviewed: changelog (RU/ES 0.21.0 section), commands (--client-id; copied from the released reference), configuration (the sign-in order list, the events keys the api methods also need), installation (WireCat's app in every package, --client-id, google_client_id), troubleshooting (the oauth_client null row, the missing-secret row, the unverified app row), usage (the sign-in order). Index, remote, scenarios and security unchanged. Roadmap: v0.21.0 dropped its only Next item (sign-in without your own client, shipped in 0.20.0) and listed no status, so the roadmap page is pinned to gcal-cli main 8167d16 (gcal-cli #133), which says nothing new is planned yet. The comparison page is checked against 0.21.0 on 7 November: no mark changes; the agent-permission note adds that the raw api events methods answer to the same events keys. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.20.0 (Core 0.566.0/Base 0.77.1). 0.20.0 renames error reasons to the names cli-core and drive share (sign-in.expired is oauth.expired, sign-in.scope-missing and api.scope-missing are oauth.scope-missing, profile.not-signed-in is oauth.missing, google.denied is access.denied, google.not-found is item.not-found, google.usage-limit is provider.usage-limit). calendars busy takes and answers starts_at and ends_at. A sync where one calendar fails saves and answers the others with meta.complete false and a sync.partial issue, exit 0. cli-core 0.566.0 adds the conflict failure (exit 15), and doctor connects nowhere unless doctor --online. gcal signs in with WireCat's Google app from cli-core's constants.json with no client file (order: --client-file, then GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, then WireCat's app), a secret without an id fails with sign-in.secret-without-id, sign-in.no-client and sign-in.bundled-client-invalid are gone, and doctor's oauth_client is {client, source}. Also: config migrate and config repair, events create --text retries with --operation-id, session start opens no browser under --json, --no-input or CI, reads open the store read-only, Google paging stops after a repeated token or 1000 pages, events export --output writes a private file whole, organizer-only changes say event.organizer-only, local times at a terminal, and busy says when Google did not answer. EN/RU/ES pages reviewed: changelog (RU/ES translated), commands (calendars busy fields, doctor --online, config migrate and repair, exit 15), usage (partial sync, busy fields, quick add retry), remote (the example tunnel address), troubleshooting (oauth.scope-missing). gcal's own installation, configuration, usage, troubleshooting and roadmap pages at v0.20.0 still say releases do not carry WireCat's app, so portal corrections in EN/RU/ES now say every package carries it, that Google has not verified it yet (unverified app page, 100 users in total shared with drive), and that your own app is the way out. Troubleshooting drops the rows for errors 0.20.0 cannot give (unreadable bundled client, no client set up, oauth_client.client null), adds sign-in.secret-without-id. The owner confirmed a real sign-in through WireCat's app with the Calendar API on, so the pages drop the hedges that doubted it. The changelog correction names oauth.missing and provider.usage-limit where 0.20.0's Fixed section still names the old reasons. Shared installation and agents pages say gcal signs in through WireCat's app or your own. Index, scenarios and security unchanged. Roadmap changed through the correction: sign-in without your own client ships, Google's review of WireCat's app is what stays next. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.19.0 (Core 0.551.0/Base 0.75.1). 0.19.0 installs wcat-gcal beside gcal and answers wcat-gcal --wcat-describe, so wcat gcal runs the tool and wcat --help lists it; gcal keeps working. cli-base 0.75.1 offers word* and ranges in a stored list's help only when a field takes them; every gcal list is filtered by Google and already said only what it takes, so gcal's help does not change. RU/ES changelog reviewed; other pages unchanged. Roadmap unchanged. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.18.0 (Core 0.551.0/Base 0.75.0). 0.18.0 adds docs/remote.md, a guide for ChatGPT or Claude in the browser or on the phone: Tailscale Funnel or a named Cloudflare tunnel, mcp serve --http --public-url, the one-time login code, permissions over MCP (ask runs, so --permission api=readonly or api.calendar.acl=deny for that server), mcp server start in the background, and mcp revoke; the overview and usage link to it. Outlook and Exchange feeds that name Windows time zones are read in the matching IANA zone (cli-core 0.551.0); provider-filtered lists no longer offer OR in --help (cli-base 0.75.0); the mcp serve --http login page names your Google Calendar. EN/RU/ES remote (new, in the sidebar under Guides), index, usage and changelog reviewed; other guides unchanged. Roadmap changed: What works today now names all accounts in one list, overlaps, events prepare, quick add, .ics export and import, feeds, search all and schedule, and the Next item links installation for your own Google app; sign-in without your own Google client stays next, waiting for Google app review. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.17.0 (Core 0.549.0/Base 0.74.0), covering 0.15.0 and 0.16.0. 0.15.0: schedule command <name> --every <duration> -- <gcal words> installs a systemd user timer, a launchd agent or a Task Scheduler task (schedule list, run, remove look after it), so the events remind timer is one command; installing it does not lift events.remind.hook, the command says so and gives the config set line, GCAL_READ_ONLY refuses schedule command and remove, and no MCP tool offers schedule; cron and hand-written timers stay under By hand. 0.16.0: calendars add <url> [--title] follows an iCalendar feed (https://, http:// or webcal://) as a read-only calendar of the profile, read again by sync, with repeating events expanded in their own time zone; its events show in events list, search events, overlapping:true and events remind, a write refuses with calendar.read-only before anything is sent, calendars busy leaves feeds out, and the address is kept in the keyring (gcal-cli / feeds:<profile>) or credentials.json and never printed; calendars add and remove are not on MCP. A write to a calendar shared as reader now refuses with calendar.read-only, and the --client-file reader moved to cli-core with unchanged shapes and errors. 0.17.0: search all <query> searches stored meetings, the other tools' messages and notes in one ranked list (kind and ref per hit, meta.accounts, --only, --source, --limit, --page, --exact, --timezone; transcripts only when --source names a meeting account; --only mail refuses and points to memo search mail), over MCP as a read with permissions.search.all; sync asks a feed with ETag/Last-Modified and keeps stored events when nothing changed (feeds unchanged: true), the first sync of a day and --rescan read in full; calendars add warns once on stderr for http://; calendars remove now deletes the feed calendar and its events (may break callers). RU/ES changelog, usage (Follow a calendar feed, Search everything at once, Run it on a timer with Keep feeds fresh and By hand), commands and security reviewed; scenarios, index, installation, configuration, troubleshooting and roadmap unchanged. A correction marks the usage guide's words after which a scheduled command is typed as gcal personal …, which the command checker read as an unknown command. The comparison adds a row for following a calendar published as an .ics address (gcal yes, the other tools not in their documentation), keeps one search over meetings, chats, mail and notes as partly because mail goes to memo search mail, adds schedule to the reminders note, a calendar feeds note, and names calendars add, remove and schedule among the commands kept at a terminal. Roadmap unchanged since 0.14.0: Next is still only sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app; What works today does not yet name feeds, search all or schedule, which is incomplete but not wrong. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.14.0 (Core 0.543.0/Base 0.73.0), covering 0.13.0. 0.13.0: events list, events prepare, doctor and session status carry meta.now, meta.now_local and meta.timezone (WC-TIME-7), and the skill tells the agent to plan from them; over MCP a list's query names its fields and says -event_type:<kind> or NOT event_type:<kind> leaves a kind out; events export without --output runs through gcal_read, so a read-only profile (GCAL_READ_ONLY) can export, while --output stays off MCP and the read-only lock refuses it. 0.14.0: events remind [--due-within 10m, 1m to 1d] [--dry-run] [--offline] [-- <program> ...], for cron, a systemd timer, launchd or Task Scheduler, syncs, then tells once about each timed event that starts within the window (not cancelled, declined, focus, out-of-office or working-location; a moved meeting is reminded again); a failed sync still reminds from the store with meta.complete: false and exits with the sync's code. The program runs with no shell, once per event, the event as one JSON line on stdin with ref and untrusted, GCAL_EVENT and GCAL_PROFILE in its environment; exit 0 marks it reminded, any other leaves it for the next run (remind.hook-failed), 60 seconds stops it, and a second run at once answers remind.running. permissions.events.remind.hook defaults to deny, --yes does not lift it, GCAL_READ_ONLY refuses it, and no MCP tool offers events remind. RU/ES changelog, usage (Get reminded before a meeting, the time in answers, export through gcal_read), commands, security and roadmap reviewed; scenarios unchanged. The comparison adds a row for a reminder through your own program (gcal and gcalcli yes) and notes on the time in answers, reminders and their safety rules, and read-only export; three commands now stay off MCP. Roadmap changed: What works today names events remind; Next is still only sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.12.0 (Core 0.539.0/Base 0.71.0). events prepare [event:<id>] gives the stored evidence for one meeting, the next one when none is named (timed, not cancelled or declined, not focus, out-of-office or working-location, with someone else invited): the event with attendees' answers and Drive files, and per attendee linked identities, latest one-to-one messages and mail, group messages, past events and recorded meetings from every WireCat tool on the computer; it reads the store only and writes no summary, meta.complete: false names chat.not-read or meetings.index-pending, untrusted marks other people's text. The skill and gcal guide gain prepare-meeting and digest. events create --text hands one line to Google's quickAdd (keys events.create and api.calendar.events.quickAdd, no --operation-id). events export <query> [--output file.ics] writes up to 1000 events in UTC, one per occurrence; events import <calendar> <file> adds up to 500 events under their UIDs through events.import, mails nobody and asks first (events.import ask). events list takes event_type:<kind> and -event_type:<kind> (the only field a minus can leave out) and id:<id>; calendars are named by title everywhere, a shared name refused with calendar.ambiguous. RU/ES changelog, usage, commands and scenarios (new digest and prepare-meeting) reviewed; the comparison marks preparing for the next meeting as yes and adds rows for leaving out birthdays and working-location blocks and for .ics export and import. Roadmap unchanged since 0.7.0: sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app is still planned. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.11.0 (Core 0.527.0/Base 0.68.1). events list --source reads several accounts as one list (all, a provider, gcal:<profile>,... or group:<name>): meta.accounts names them, a meeting two accounts hold is listed once, an account with no synced calendar or an unfinished sync makes the answer partial (meta.complete: false, calendar.unsynced or calendar.sync-incomplete), and GCAL_PROFILE_LOCK limits --source to the locked profile. events list overlapping:true keeps timed meetings that overlap another, each with overlaps; cancelled, declined, free, working-location and all-day events are left out and back-to-back meetings do not overlap; with --source it compares across accounts. session start can use a WireCat Google app built into the package, but 0.11.0 carries none, so every user still makes their own: the installation guide gains Make your own Google app (steps 1 to 8) and troubleshooting gains Sign-in problems. The usage guide's raw api section now matches 0.7.0 (easy-to-undo writes run without a question, deletes and sharing ask, calendars.clear, delete and transferOwnership refused until allowed). The MCP server is listed in the MCP Registry as dev.wirecat/gcal-cli from the next release. RU/ES installation, configuration, troubleshooting, usage, commands and changelog reviewed; the comparison marks all accounts in one list and overlapping meetings as yes. Roadmap unchanged since 0.7.0: sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app is still planned, and no release carries that app yet. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.10.0 (Core 0.512.0/Base 0.68.1). 0.10.0 only moves gcal to cli-core 0.512.0: no command, option, setting or MCP input changes for gcal. cli-core 0.512.0 renamed id to operation_id in its shared calendar MCP tools and gave events_list a page, but gcal does not serve those tools; its agents use gcal_write and gcal_read, which already take operation_id and events list --page since 0.9.0. Roadmap matches the release: moving an event to another calendar and changing this-and-following occurrences shipped and left Next; sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app is still planned.

mail.conclusion: Reviewed mail 0.17.0 (cli-core 0.587.0, cli-base 0.80.0) from the changelog and the docs diff since v0.16.3. Added: messages reset moves a holder's mark back, messages restore --write undoes one write of a run, every write answers with an operation_id under writes, account inspect and messages import name the time zone of --since-time, schedule list gives the cost caps. May break callers: a change run is run_id (restore gives run_id and restored_run_id), sync, messages import and messages export take --max-messages instead of --limit, messages export takes --output-dir instead of --output, attachments download takes [attachment...]. Fixed: status on an older store schema, messages import stops cleanly, local times on screens, answers after the connection closes, eleven more registered refusal reasons, example values instead of placeholders in the user pages. The roadmap changed in wording only: the app password providers are a link to the providers page, and the rules sentence no longer says they moved from memo. Its only Next item, a live test of Gmail over OAuth, has not shipped, and no item that shipped in 0.17.0 is listed as planned. RU/ES changelog, commands, configuration, Microsoft sign-in, Outlook, providers, roadmap and usage translated and accepted. The site's own email page now names --max-messages for sync in EN, RU and ES.

b24.conclusion: Reviewed b24 v0.5.0 with its published changelog and command reference. 0.5.0 moves deals, leads, pipelines and stages to cli-core's shared CRM commands over a local store filled by sync (changes since the last sync, or everything with --rescan, deletions found once a day), adds deals and leads close and delete, moves deals and leads to refs (deal:12, lead:7), takes custom fields by label from the stored definitions, and lets search all find deals and leads beside other WireCat data, leaving out kinds the list keys deny. It removes --operation-id from every write, since a live portal made a second record for a repeated Idempotency-Key, and fixes every sync after the first, which the portal refused over the time format. The roadmap is the first one: a sales funnel board, contacts and companies from the local store and their custom fields kept locally are next; local app sign-in with an event queue, activities, quotes, smart invoices and processes, a duplicate check, CSV and a desktop Deals page come later.
